chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Bawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, who said: Abu Imran al-Ijli narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Ala' al-Khaffaf narrated to us, saying: 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi narrated, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"I did not say, nor did those who spoke before me say, anything like: 'There is no god but Allah.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (the core declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: Why is the declaration 'La ilaha illa Allah' considered superior to all other words?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this hadith in the context of the spiritual hierarchy of divine words, highlighting 'La ilaha illa Allah' as the foundational key to Islamic theology. The narration, transmitted through a chain including the reliable al-Barqi, underscores the phrase's unique ontological weight, distinguishing it from other prophetic declarations and establishing it as the core of gnosis (ma'rifah) in Shia tradition.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn ibn Husayn ibn Musa ibn Bawayh al-Qummi (ra) said: my father (ra) said, that Sa’d ibn `Abdullah informed us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu `Abdullah al-Barqi said: Abu `Imran al-`Ijli said: Muhammad ibn Sinan said: Abu al-`Ala al-Khaffaf said: `Atiyyah al-`Awfi said, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, he said that The Messenger of Allah (sw) said: “
Neither I nor anyone before me has said anything (with such worth) like: `There is no god but Allah’ [La ilaha illa Allah].”
